metadata.name: checkwash
metadata.summary: Flags known patterns of weakened tests and CI checks in a Git diff.
metadata.description:
# CheckWash

CheckWash reads your Git diff and flags changes that weaken tests or CI checks.
For example, changing `assert total == 105.3` to `assert total > 0` lets an
incorrect total pass. CheckWash flags the relaxed assertion for review.

Use the [latest verified installation guide](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/install.md)
for the recommended Python package version, standalone download, and GitHub
Action commit to pin in your workflow.
The Action uses the CheckWash version at that commit. Upgrading your local
CLI and updating the workflow pin are separate steps.

After installing the CLI, run `python -m checkwash demo` to see sample findings.
Run `python -m checkwash check` in your Git repository to check your uncommitted
changes. See the [project README](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash#readme)
for usage examples and CI setup.

CheckWash is alpha. Legitimate refactors can trigger a block. For example,
the 0.12.0 CLI blocked 6 of 60 cases in the project's refactor corpus,
including 4 of the 57 strictly qualified cases. See the
[measurement details and known limits](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/fbae5f7d4b9bd4b891ac7fe962401f2bda1483f4/README.md#know-the-limits).
